newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler, GM report April sales declines.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler, GM report April sales declines.

text.p: Chrysler Corp., feeling the effects of an engine plant strike, Thursday reported an 11.5 percent drop in U.S. sales for April, while General Motors Corp. reported a smaller decline.
GM, the largest U.S. automaker, reported an April sales decline of 5.2 percent as total car and truck sales fell to 418,173 from 441,254, in part because of its own labour troubles.
GM's car sales were 236,562, a 12.6 percent decline from last year. Total truck sales rose 6.5 percent to 181,611 from 170,502.
GM said its new models were continuing to gain acceptance, but April sales were hurt by strikes at its Malibu car plant in Oklahoma City, Okla., and a full-size pickup truck plant in Pontiac, Mich.

Chrysler finished April with total sales of 204,080, down from last year's all-time April record of 230,469. Light truck sales were 134,166, down 9.8 percent from 148,768 a year ago. Car sales tumbled almost 14 percent to 69,914.

"There's intense competition for car buyers as the market softens with the industry shift toward the light truck segment," said James Holden, Chrysler's executive vice president of sales and marketing. "The softening is affecting all the major manufacturers, and Chrysler is no exception.
Holden also said a three-week old strike at the No. 3 U.S. automaker's Mound Road Engine plant in Detroit has caused "short-term uncertainty."
Toyota Motor Corp., however, reported record April U.S. sales of 98,071 cars and light trucks, an increase of 9.7 percent from a year ago.

Toyota's total car sales, riding the strength of record Camry demand, jumped 12.3 percent to 68,390. Total sport utility vehicle sales were up 7.8 percent to 16,675. Pickup truck sales rose 1.8 percent to 12,505.
